newsitem.title: UK: Chiroscience anaesthetic works in childbirth.
newsitem.headline: Chiroscience anaesthetic works in childbirth.

text.p: Drug discovery company Chiroscience Group Plc said on Tuesday that preliminary results of late-stage trials showed that its fast-acting local anaesthetic Levobupivacaine works "in line with expectations" in childbirth.
The company said in a statement that it would present initial results of its first Phase III trial of Levobupivacaine in obstetrics to a conference in Bermuda on Wednesday.

Chiroscience said a trial involving 60 patients at St James's Hospital in Leeds showed that patients required an almost identical quantity of Levobupivacaine to control pain as of bupivacaine, the generic drug from which the Chiroscience product is derived.
The company has developed a single isomer version of bupivacaine, which it believes has fewer side effects than the original drug.

"These results are exactly what we wanted to see from this trial, reinforcing our product positioning of superior safety together with the desired potency profile," said Brian Gennery, director of development at Chiroscience.
Shares in the company rose 14 pence to 380 pence after the announcement.

Analysts said the company is conducting more than a dozen Phase III trials of the drug in a variety of uses, with a European approval application expected by the end of 1997 and a U.S. filing expected by the middle of 1998.
